base: vintage 19th-century storybook pen-and-ink engraving, black and white line art, fine cross-hatching and stippling, etching illustration, clean off-white background, light airy line art, mostly white, pure line art (NOT watercolor, no grey wash, NOT dark). WIDE HORIZONTAL LANDSCAPE orientation, 3:2 aspect ratio, much wider than tall. RECURRING CHARACTER (must look identical in every image): an anthropomorphic European mole as a Victorian gentleman-businessman: stout rounded body with velvety dark fur, pointed pink snout, tiny eyes behind small round wire-rimmed spectacles, broad digging paws, three-piece tweed suit, long overcoat, bowler hat, leather briefcase. SECOND RECURRING CHARACTER (when mentioned): an anthropomorphic white heron as an elegant Victorian businesswoman: tall slender body, long neck and long legs, calm sharp gaze, sober tailored Victorian work dress with the hem lifted and sleeves rolled up. Setting: a cobblestone medieval-European fairytale town with half-timbered Tudor houses, enormous twisted old trees, a river, lamp posts; other anthropomorphic animals (rabbits, badgers, birds, foxes) as townsfolk in period clothing may appear in the background. IMPORTANT SCALE RULE: all characters share a consistent, realistic relative scale — the mole is a small-to-medium sized townsfolk, the SAME size as the rabbits and badgers, never larger than the other animals or the buildings around him. Whimsical, elegant, highly detailed. NO text, NO words, NO letters, NO signage, NO numbers, NO logos, no color.

images.scene: Medium shot: the mole businessman standing proudly in the town square at the foot of a gigantic ancient tree whose massive trunk extends out of the top of the frame, holding his leather briefcase, a few townsfolk animals in the background.

Cutaway cross-section view: above ground, the cobblestone street of the town with half-timbered houses; below ground, the mole's immaculate network of tunnels, with the mole businessman working at the center among root cellars and stored burlap sacks. The mole is SMALL, exactly the same body size as the townsfolk animals walking on the street above; his tunnel chambers are modest burrow-sized rooms, much smaller than the houses above. Two worlds in one frame.

A four-panel storybook comic grid, two rows of two square panels with thin decorative frames, no captions: top-left the mole digging vigorously with his broad paws in a tunnel; top-right the mole opening and inspecting stacked burlap sacks in a storeroom; bottom-left the mole propping a wooden support beam against a tunnel ceiling; bottom-right the mole examining thick tree roots with his spectacles almost touching them, oil lantern raised. IMPORTANT OVERRIDE FOR THIS IMAGE ONLY: SQUARE 1:1 format, exactly as tall as it is wide, NOT landscape.

Cinematic EXTREME CLOSE-UP in profile, macro shot: the mole's face fills the frame, his pointed pink snout PRESSED almost against the gnarled bark of a thick tree root, round wire spectacles catching the warm glow of an oil lantern just out of frame, individual hairs of his velvety fur and the deep cracked texture of the root bark rendered in obsessive fine hatching, floating dust motes in the lantern light. Intimate, proud, concentrated expression. Background dissolves to plain paper white.

ONE single continuous cinematic scene, side-view cross-section at ground level (no split-screen, no dividing line): below the soil line, the mole's neat freshly dug tunnel runs toward the roots of an orchard; above the soil line, the orchard trees stand completely dead and withered, bare cracked branches against a pale empty sky, shriveled fruit fallen on the dry cracked earth. The mole appears exactly ONCE in the image: emerging at the tunnel's end at the base of a dead tree, seen from BEHIND, bowler hat in paw, looking up at the ruin; the tunnel behind him is empty. The heron does NOT appear in this image, no birds in clothing. The contrast between the proud tunnel below and the dead orchard above tells the story.

Dramatic top-down zenithal view looking straight down into a deep tunnel shaft: at the very bottom, small, the lone mole digging by lantern light, surrounded by earth on all sides. Edges of the frame stay light and airy, mostly white paper.

Medium shot at the riverbank: the elegant heron businesswoman in her tailored Victorian work dress with hem lifted, standing in the shallow muddy water among reeds, working hard gathering fish into a wicker basket; a few other animal workers in the background. Elegant but clearly hard at work. The mole does NOT appear in this image.

Wide shot at dusk, light sky: in the foreground the mole businessman at the mouth of his burrow with earth on his paws, gazing toward the background where the heron businesswoman works with her feet in the mud at the riverbank. Two workers in the same frame, the distance between them is the subject.

Strong vertical composition: the heron taking flight from the riverbank, wide wings spread, rising above the treetops; below, small and discreet, the mole businessman watching from his burrow entrance.

Dynamic hero shot from a low angle: the heron in full flight carrying the mole businessman clinging to her back and holding his bowler hat, the two breaking above the treetop line, the little town shrinking below. Wind, height, vertigo.

Bird's-eye aerial view of the whole forest far below: a river making a wide bend, one side of the forest dense and alive, the other side thin and dying with bare trees; in a corner of the frame, a SINGLE lone heron in flight carrying the mole on her back, tiny in the frame. No crowd, no other birds, no other animals flying.

Intimate close-up high in the sky: the mole RIDING ON THE HERON'S BACK in mid-flight (part of the heron's white feathered back and one wide wing visible beneath him filling the lower frame), the mole gripping her feathers, wind in his velvety fur, round spectacles, tiny eyes wide open in awe at the immensity out of frame, clouds and faint treetops far below. Revelation on his face. The mole is NOT flying by himself, he has no wings.

Aerial view in detail: below, a dried-out orchard of bare fruit trees right next to an old dry riverbed; in the distance, the river's new course carrying water to the other side of the forest. Above the scene glides a SINGLE heron carrying the mole on her back, the mole pointing down at the dry riverbed with his paw. No other animals in the sky.

Two panels side by side, thin decorative border, no captions: first panel, the mole back in his tunnels digging steadily with his broad paws, firm and content; second panel, the same mole standing at the top of a hill at dawn, looking over the entire forest and pointing a direction with his paw.

Serene monumental scene, seen from behind at a three-quarter angle: the mole businessman and the heron businesswoman standing side by side at the top of a hill, the entire fairytale town and forest open before them at sunrise, the river crossing the landscape.

Final scene at dawn: the prosperous fairytale town alive: the river running, the orchard blooming again with white blossoms, townsfolk animals busy in the streets; in the foreground the mole businessman standing confident on a small hill with his briefcase, overlooking it all.
